newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian court throws out opposition petition.
newsitem.headline: Zambian court throws out opposition petition.

text.p: A Zambian court on Thursday threw out an opposition petition challenging President Frederick Chiluba's eligibility to stand for president in disputed polls scheduled for Monday.
"The law is clear. A petition against the election of a president can only be made after the winning candidate is sworn into office," Chief Justice Mathew Ngulube told Zambia's highest court.

The petitioners, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party (UNIP), allege that Chiluba lied about his nationality and parentage on his electoral nomination papers.
Chiluba said in his papers that he was born in Zambia's northern Copperbelt province to Zambian parents.
The petitioners, however, claim to have evidence that he was born outside Zambia and told reporters they would resume their challenge after the elections.
